Inference for summary statistics of fitted effects

Source: R/effect-inference.R
effect_inference.Rd

Estimates, interval-estimates, and tests summary statistics of one or more fitted effects, such as contrasts between groups, areas under an impulse-response function, averages over observed covariates, or peak lags. Every effect is evaluated as in estimate_effect(), and all of them are evaluated on one joint distribution of the coefficients they use, so summaries that combine effects with shared coefficients have the right variance.

Usage

effect_inference(
  object,
  effects,
  estimand = NULL,
  null = 0,
  method = c("auto", "wald", "simulation", "delta"),
  level = 0.95,
  draws = 2000L,
  seed = NULL,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  boundary = c("estimate", "bound"),
  impulses = NULL,
  responses = NULL,
  keep_draws = FALSE
)

Arguments

object

A fitted cdrgam model.

effects

A named list of effect specifications. Each is a list with any of terms, axes, composition, grouping, groups, reference, n, and points, as in estimate_effect().

estimand

NULL, a matrix with one row per estimand and one column per effect row (effects stacked in order), a named list whose elements are lists of weights named by effect (a weight of length one is recycled over that effect's rows), or a function. A function receives a named list of numeric effect values and a named list of effect grids, and returns a numeric vector, named to label the estimands.

null

The value of each estimand under the null hypothesis, of length one or one per estimand.

method

"auto" uses Wald inference for linear estimands and simulation for function estimands. "delta" applies only to function estimands.

level

Confidence level for lower and upper.

draws

Number of coefficient draws for simulation, and of Gaussian draws for simultaneous critical values.

seed

Optional seed. The previous random state is restored.

unconditional

Include smoothing-parameter uncertainty when supported. Smoothing parameters classified as on the boundary of their range contribute no uncertainty, because the criterion has no local curvature along them. Sparse fits stop with an error when the outer Hessian is not positive definite after those parameters are excluded.

boundary

"estimate" (the default) uses the fitted smoothing parameters. "bound" repeats the calculation with each boundary smoothing parameter set to its profile bound, the largest variance component the data still support, while the other smoothing parameters stay at their estimates. Compare the two to check whether conclusions depend on treating those variance components as zero. "bound" requires a sparse Gaussian REML fit with sparse_control$boundary_sensitivity = TRUE and unconditional = FALSE.

impulses, responses

Optional training streams used to recover axis summaries from models fitted before summaries were stored.

keep_draws

If TRUE, store the estimand draws of a simulation as attribute draws, with one row per estimand.

Value

A cdrgam_effect_inference data frame with one row per estimand: estimand, estimate, std_error, lower, upper, null, statistic (the standardized difference from null), p_value, simultaneous_lower, simultaneous_upper, adjusted_p_value, and method. Attributes hold covariance, the estimand covariance; joint_test, a Wald test that every estimand equals its null; grids, the effect grids with their estimates; level; and draws when kept.

Details

The effects are a linear map D beta of the coefficients. A linear estimand L D beta has covariance L D V D' L', and Wald inference is exact given the Gaussian approximation to the coefficient posterior. Give it as a matrix or a list of weights, or leave estimand NULL to make every effect row an estimand.

A function estimand is nonlinear in general. method = "simulation" draws beta ~ N(beta-hat, V) and applies the function to each draw. The estimate is the function at beta-hat, the standard error is the standard deviation of the draws, the interval uses their quantiles, and the p-value is the two-sided posterior tail area beyond null, whose resolution is 1 / draws. method = "delta" instead linearizes the function at the estimate by central differences. It is invalid for functions that are not differentiable there, such as maxima and argmaxima.

Simultaneous intervals and adjusted p-values cover all estimands of one call. They use the maximum over estimands of the standardized absolute deviation, from Gaussian draws with the estimand correlation for Wald and delta inference, or from the coefficient draws for simulation. The adjusted p-values are single-step max-modulus p-values, estimated from those draws and never below the unadjusted p-value.
